evals.name: generic-edit-command
evals.prompt: From discovery we have a screen 'Edit locker' with a form that calls `UpdateLocker` (name, size, location, volume) and produces `LockerUpdated`. Review this command and event design and propose a better one. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A form verb (Update, Edit, Save, Set, Change, Manage + noun) means several decisions share a form. Ask which separate business reasons change these values and split into imperative business commands such as ReassignLocker and CorrectLockerVolume, each producing a specific past-tense event such as LockerRelocated or VolumeCorrected. Never `XUpdated`/`Changed`/`Edited`.
assertions: Flags `UpdateLocker` as a form-verb command that hides several decisions.
Splits it by the separate business reasons the values change, with imperative names like ReassignLocker or CorrectLockerVolume.
Replaces `LockerUpdated` with specific past-tense events such as LockerRelocated or VolumeCorrected.
Says an event must not be named XUpdated, Changed, Edited or Saved.

evals.name: stored-state-rule
evals.prompt: On Screenplay 4.198.0, rule: a member may have at most 3 active loans. MemberLoans is a finite event-log projection keyed directly by the member event source with removal handling; memberId is a required String concept input. Stage is 4.126.0. The draft BorrowBook command takes an input `activeLoanCount` from the UI and `require activeLoanCount < 3`, plus an input `confirmsEligible == true`. Review it and show the correct modeling. Give the code or outline in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Reject caller-supplied state and attestation inputs. Declare application-root command reads protected, reads MemberLoans as loans by memberId and require loans.activeCount < 3 with indented message. This selects v25; absent required state rejects Validation before requirements, matching intervening facts return Conflict/DecisionStateChanged with no facts. Do not add concurrency (PLAY0783); legacy reads without opt-in remain PLAY0271. Stage admits v25 but refuses protected reads STAGE-ESM-044, so separately verify target consistency. Never claim payload-key fan-in or arbitrary projections qualify.
assertions: Rejects the caller-supplied `activeLoanCount` input because state must not be copied into the command.
Rejects the boolean attestation input `confirmsEligible == true` standing in for a rule.
Writes application-root command reads protected, aliased keyed read and require over stored count with an indented message, selecting v25.
Explains absence Validation and matching intervening fact Conflict/DecisionStateChanged without facts; does not combine reads/concurrency or admit payload-key fan-in.
Names Stage STAGE-ESM-044 for protected reads despite v25 version admission and separates reference protection from target realization instead of claiming reads are always unprotected.

evals.name: events-or-views
evals.prompt: Stakeholders want to see (a) whether a loan is 'overdue', (b) the quoted rental price the customer was shown, and (c) a running total of fines. Decide for each whether it is an event or a view in the Screenplay model and why. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Ask whether the value was decided or supplied (event) or can be worked out from recorded facts (view). Time-relative states like 'overdue' are not stored: store the deadline and compute. A decided calculation such as a quoted price is a fact. A running figure is a view, never an `XRecalculated` event.
assertions: Treats 'overdue' as a view over a stored deadline, not a stored state or event.
Treats the quoted price as a fact (event) because it is a decided calculation.
Treats the running fines total as a view and says never to model it as an `XRecalculated` event.
States the test: decided or supplied is an event; derivable from already-recorded facts is a view.

evals.name: acting-screen
evals.prompt: Our Level-1 screen 'ApproveRefund' has only `action ApproveRefund` and no data lines. A second screen 'RegisterBoat' has an action and no data. A third has neither. Which are acceptable? Also the list screen's query takes `filter ownerId` from the UI so users see only their rows. Review all of that. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A screen acting on an existing instance needs `data` from a view that supplies the identifier and the state the user decides on; only a creation screen may lack `data` and says so in the slice description. A screen with neither `data` nor `action` is a gap. Whose rows is part of the view; a caller-supplied filter is not access control.
assertions: Says ApproveRefund, acting on an existing instance, needs `data` from a view that supplies the identifier and decision state.
Accepts RegisterBoat lacking `data` only as a creation screen and only if the slice `description` says so.
Says a screen with neither `data` nor `action` is a gap.
Says a caller-supplied `filter ownerId` is not access control, because whose rows a view shows is part of the view's design.
